messages:
Maya (sales): NovaHealth follow-up: netsec insists on SNI visibility to their DMZ inspector and original client IP in app logs. They asked if we can avoid peering because of org rules. Can we preserve client IP + SNI using anything other than peering? Need a short answer + a one-line cost delta for 5TB.

Ike (solutions): Short answer: if they forbid peering, we can still support SNI + client-id visibility but it requires customer-side proxying (they terminate TLS in DMZ, re-TLS to a customer proxy that forwards XFF) or using a transparent inline approach with GWLB + a probe that preserves srcip to our backend. Both involve customer infra changes.

Zoe (neteng): A few concrete paths:
1) Peering (native): preserves src IP, SNI seen by DMZ if TLS terminates before peering. Lowest friction for logs.
2) PrivateLink (interface endpoint): isolates VPCs, but endpoint ENIs NAT; client IPs appear as ENI IPs unless customer proxy injects X-Forwarded-For. SNI is not visible to their inspector after PrivateLink unless TLS is terminated earlier.
3) GWLB + transparent proxy in customer VPC: push traffic through their gateway load balancer + inline proxy that can mirror SNI and forward original src IP to our peered path or re-TLS to us. This is more complex but keeps isolation and gives inspector visibility.

Zoe (neteng): Quick ASCII: 
OnPrem -> DMZ TLS Inspector -> Customer Proxy (terminate) -> TGW/spoke -> Peering -> Redwood
OnPrem -> DMZ TLS Inspector -> GWLB -> Inline Proxy -> InterfaceEndpoint/GWLB -> Redwood (proxy preserves XFF)

Diego (security): From questionnaire POV: include KMS/HSM language and note about TLS handling. Suggested wording: "Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; we do not store plaintext customer keys. When customers perform TLS inspection in their DMZ, they must terminate and re-establish TLS to Redwood; we support mTLS and audit exports of key usage."

Maya (sales): Cost one-liner? They want a simple comparison to paste in SOW for 5TB/mo.

Ike (solutions): One-liner (ballpark): PrivateLink infra fees ~ $0.01/hr endpoint + ~$0.01/GB data processing => ~ $50-70/mo for 5TB (ex cloud provider egress). Peering: no endpoint fee; cross-VPC transfer ~$0.005-$0.02/GB => ~$25-100/mo. GWLB/proxy path adds customer infra and proxy processing costs (depends on appliance), expect additional hourly+data processing costs; flag as engineering integration item.

Zoe (neteng): Firewall snippet to hand ops (paste-ready):
```
# PrivateLink
Allow TCP/443 -> <interface-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>
# VPC Peering
Allow TCP/443 -> <redwood-peering-cidr>
# GWLB/Proxy (customer-side)
Allow TCP/443 -> <gwlb-endpoint-subnet-cidrs>
# Common
Enforce TLS >=1.2; deny weak ciphers. If proxying, ensure X-Forwarded-For header is preserved and logged.
```

Maya (sales): Any enterprise blockers to call out before we send SOW?

Diego (security): Blockers: 1) If customer policy forbids any ENI allowlists our PrivateLink onboarding will stall. 2) If they require inspected SNI + original srcIP WITH strictly end-to-end TLS (no termination) that's impossible; must choose which they relax. 3) Air-gapped/regulatory needs may force on-prem package and longer lead time.

Ike (solutions): I'll draft a 1-paragraph SOW blurb recommending the peering default with an alternative path and cost delta.

oncall-bot: Created RW-4599: "NovaHealth - network topology decision (SNI + srcIP) + cost delta" and attached runbook stub.

Maya (sales): Thanks team 44d. Ike, ping me the SOW paragraph and paste the firewall lines into the customer email.
